sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, "Uno Friends" is a simple card game that's easy to learn but still offers a lot of depth and complexity. The game is played with a standard deck of Uno cards, which features a unique combination of colors, numbers, and special action cards. The objective of the game is to be the first player to get rid of all your cards, and the game is won by the player who achieves this goal.

The gameplay is divided into two main phases: the draw phase and the discard phase. During the draw phase, players draw a card from the deck and add it to their hand. During the discard phase, players take turns playing cards from their hand onto a discard pile. The twist is that players must match the color or number of the card on top of the discard pile, or they can play a special action card to change the rules of the game.

The game also features a variety of special action cards, including reverse, skip, and draw two cards. These cards can be used to disrupt the flow of the game and gain an advantage over your opponents. For example, the reverse card can switch the direction of play, while the skip card can force another player to skip their turn. The draw two card, on the other hand, can force another player to draw two cards from the deck and skip their turn.

Overall, the core gameplay mechanics of "Uno Friends" are simple yet engaging, making it a great game for players of all ages and skill levels.
